title: Distributed systems and cloud computing
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Understand how to build systems that run on many machines: partial failure, RPC and messaging, logical clocks and ordering, mutual exclusion and leader election, replication and consistency models, consensus with Paxos and Raft, fault tolerance and the CAP theorem, partitioning and consistent hashing, batch and stream processing, cloud service models, containers, orchestration and observability.
primary_reading: Distributed Systems by van Steen and Tanenbaum, 4th edition (free digital copy)

weeks.1: What makes distributed systems hard: partial failure
weeks.3: Time, clocks and ordering: Lamport and vector clocks
weeks.8: Fault tolerance and the CAP theorem
weeks.9: Partitioning, consistent hashing and distributed storage
weeks.10: Batch and stream processing: MapReduce and beyond
weeks.11: Cloud computing: IaaS, PaaS and serverless

blocks.deliverable: Classify the failures in five scenarios.
Assign Lamport and vector timestamps to a trace.
Decide which consistency models allow supplied histories.
Week 7 midterm; trace a Raft election and log replication.
Write a MapReduce word count and trace it.
Design a deployment for a supplied service.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Distributed systems simulation: implement in Python a simulated key-value store replicated with a simplified Raft-style leader and log, inject crashes and lost messages, show that committed writes survive, and write a design report.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
